comment: The technology catalog: every option an application specification (src/appspec.js) can select, with its category, support status, compatibility and how it is generated, integrated, verified and detected. Package names and versions are NOT here: an entry that brings packages names its component in templates/stack.json ("stack"), which stays the single source for pins, package rules and the stack gate. status: supported = generated, integrated and verified by the factory; constrained = supported only under the stated constraint; planned = catalog-only (named so it can be detected in existing repositories and shown with its blocker, never executable). Verification kinds: checklist = an existing completion checklist item, command = a command that must exit 0, file = a file that must exist (presence, not behaviour).

entries.name: Full-stack web
entries.description: One Node.js process serves the HTTP API, the AppPort boundary and the browser UI.

entries.name: API / backend service
entries.constraint: Built by the model agents (the offline templates always include a UI); verified by its tests, a health check and the AppPort gate.
entries.description: An HTTP API and AppPort boundary with no browser UI.
rules: Architecture: an API service with no browser UI. Do not create public/ or any HTML page; GET / may return a JSON description of the service.

entries.name: Single-page application (no backend)
entries.description: A browser-only app with no server of its own.
entries.blocker: With no server there is no process to host the AppPort boundary, and the factory's verification (tests, preview health check, AppPort gate) needs one. The factory's single-page UIs are served by a full-stack app instead.
entries.next: Decide where a browser-only app's capabilities live (a separate AppPort host or none, with an exception), then add a static-hosting preview check.

entries.name: Server-rendered web
entries.description: Pages rendered on the server (for example Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit).
entries.blocker: No server-rendering generator or verification exists yet.
entries.next: Add a framework generator (see the tooling entries) with a preview check of rendered pages.

entries.name: Static website
entries.description: Prebuilt pages with no application server.
entries.blocker: No static-site generator or hosting check exists; a static site has no AppPort host.
entries.next: Add a static build and preview check; decide its capability story.

entries.name: Background worker
entries.description: A long-running job processor without an HTTP UI.
entries.blocker: No worker generator, and the factory's verification starts an HTTP app and probes it.
entries.next: Add a worker template and a job-level verification.

entries.name: CLI application
entries.blocker: No CLI generator; the factory's deploy and AppPort checks assume an HTTP process.
entries.next: Add a CLI template with command-level tests.

entries.name: Desktop application
entries.blocker: No desktop packaging or UI verification exists.
entries.next: Out of scope until a packaging and UI-test path exists.

entries.name: Mobile application
entries.blocker: No mobile toolchain or device verification exists.
entries.next: Out of scope until a build and device-test path exists.

entries.name: Monorepo / multi-service
entries.description: Several services (possibly in different languages) in one repository.
entries.blocker: The factory plans, runs and verifies one application per run; there is no service graph, per-service toolchain or cross-service verification yet.
entries.next: Represent services in the specification, then verify each service with its own checks and the AppPort contract between them.

entries.name: Plain HTML, CSS and JS
entries.description: Static files in public/ with no framework or bundler (the factory's default UI).

entries.name: React
entries.constraint: Built by the model agents with Vite (no offline template); verified by npm run build producing public/index.html.
entries.description: React components bundled for the browser.

entries.name: Vue
entries.blocker: No verified Vue package pins or build rules in the factory yet.
entries.next: Pin vue and its Vite plugin in stack.json after a verified install and build, as React was.

entries.name: Svelte
entries.blocker: No verified Svelte package pins or build rules yet.
entries.next: Pin svelte and its Vite plugin after a verified install and build.

entries.name: Angular
entries.blocker: Angular brings its own CLI build; no verified pins or build rules yet.
entries.next: Pin Angular and add an Angular CLI build check.

entries.name: No build step
entries.description: UI files are served as written.

entries.name: Vite
entries.constraint: Used with React only; builds web/ into public/, which the app's server serves.

entries.name: Next.js
entries.description: React framework with server rendering and its own server.
entries.blocker: Next.js runs its own server; mounting the AppPort boundary in Next route handlers and verifying it has not been done.
entries.next: Verify an AppPort binding inside Next.js route handlers and a production build + start check, then pin it in stack.json.

entries.name: Nuxt
entries.blocker: Requires Vue support and an AppPort binding in Nitro, neither verified.
entries.next: Support Vue first, then verify an AppPort binding in Nuxt server routes.

entries.name: SvelteKit
entries.blocker: Requires Svelte support and an AppPort binding in SvelteKit endpoints, neither verified.
entries.next: Support Svelte first, then verify an AppPort binding in SvelteKit endpoints.

entries.name: Astro
entries.blocker: No verified Astro build or server integration.
entries.next: Add an Astro build check and decide where its capabilities are hosted.

entries.name: JavaScript
entries.description: ESM JavaScript on Node.js and in the browser.

entries.name: TypeScript
entries.constraint: For the Vite-built UI; the Node server stays JavaScript. Verified by tsc --noEmit.

entries.name: Python
entries.blocker: No Python generator, and there is no published Python AppPort package, so a Python app's capability boundary could not use the AppPort contract (a hand-written protocol would be a second implementation).
entries.next: A published, verified AppPort binding for Python; then Python templates with pytest verification.

entries.name: Rust
entries.blocker: No Rust generator or AppPort binding.
entries.next: A verified AppPort binding and cargo-based verification.

entries.name: Go
entries.blocker: No Go generator or AppPort binding.
entries.next: A verified AppPort binding and go test verification.

entries.name: Java
entries.blocker: No Java generator or AppPort binding.
entries.next: A verified AppPort binding and Maven/Gradle verification.

entries.name: C#
entries.blocker: No .NET generator or AppPort binding.
entries.next: A verified AppPort binding and dotnet test verification.

entries.name: Node.js
entries.description: Node.js 20 or newer runs the server and its tests.

entries.name: Browser
entries.description: The UI runs in the browser.

entries.name: Python (CPython)
entries.blocker: Only Node.js and the browser are supported runtimes; Python has no generator or AppPort binding yet (see the Python language entry).
entries.next: Support Python first.

entries.name: Rust / native / WebAssembly
entries.blocker: Only Node.js and the browser are supported runtimes; Rust has no generator or AppPort binding yet (see the Rust language entry).
entries.next: Support Rust first.

entries.name: JVM
entries.blocker: Only Node.js and the browser are supported runtimes; Java has no generator or AppPort binding yet (see the Java language entry).
entries.next: Support Java first.

entries.name: .NET
entries.blocker: Only Node.js and the browser are supported runtimes; C# has no generator or AppPort binding yet (see the C# language entry).
entries.next: Support C# first.

entries.name: Node.js http (no framework)
entries.description: The app's own node:http server: the factory's default.

entries.name: Express
entries.blocker: No verified Express pins or AppPort mounting rules yet (AppPort's Node handler takes raw req/res, which Express provides, but this has not been verified end to end).
entries.next: Verify handleNodeRequest inside an Express app with the AppPort gate, then pin express in stack.json.

entries.name: Fastify
entries.blocker: No verified Fastify pins or AppPort mounting rules.
entries.next: Verify an AppPort binding in Fastify, then pin it.

entries.name: FastAPI
entries.blocker: Python is not supported yet (no Python AppPort binding or generator).
entries.next: See Python.

entries.name: Flask
entries.blocker: Python is not supported yet.
entries.next: See Python.

entries.name: Django
entries.blocker: Python is not supported yet.
entries.next: See Python.

entries.name: No persistent storage
entries.description: State lives in the app process and is lost on restart (the factory's default store).

entries.name: FeltDB
entries.description: Durable, transactional application state with a declared data model (feltdb.flow).

entries.name: PostgreSQL
entries.blocker: Needs a database server the factory does not provision, verified client pins and migration checks.
entries.next: Provision a throwaway PostgreSQL for gates, pin a client and verify migrations.

entries.name: SQLite
entries.blocker: No verified SQLite package pins (the common Node bindings need native builds, which the factory's install skips).
entries.next: Verify node:sqlite or a prebuilt binding and a durability gate.

entries.name: MySQL
entries.blocker: Needs a database server the factory does not provision.
entries.next: As for PostgreSQL.

entries.name: External APIs (no local storage)
entries.description: The app reads and writes another service's API instead of storing data.
entries.blocker: The factory cannot verify calls to a real external API (tests run offline) and has no contract-test support for one.
entries.next: Recorded or contract-tested external APIs as part of verification.

entries.name: AppPort
entries.description: The application capability contract: declared, authorized, discoverable capabilities over the app's own store.

entries.name: AuthBoundry
entries.description: Authentication, authorization and delegation as an authority boundary.

entries.name: AppPort Services
entries.description: API keys, durable jobs, webhooks and secrets.

entries.name: Automated tests
entries.description: npm test runs the app's own test suite.

entries.name: Integration tests
entries.constraint: HTTP-level tests that start the app on port 0 inside npm test.
entries.description: Tests that drive the running app over HTTP and AppPort.
rules: Integration tests (selected): test/ contains tests that start the real app on port 0 and drive it over HTTP and AppPort; npm test runs them.

entries.name: End-to-end browser tests
entries.description: Tests that drive the UI in a real browser.
entries.blocker: Generated apps have no browser test runner the factory can install and run offline.
entries.next: Add a pinned browser runner and run it in the stack gate.

entries.name: Docker
entries.constraint: The Dockerfile is checked for presence and a HEALTHCHECK; the factory never builds or runs images.
entries.description: A Dockerfile that runs the app.

entries.name: CI/CD
entries.constraint: A GitHub Actions workflow that runs the tests is checked for presence; it is not executed by the factory.
rules: CI (selected): add .github/workflows/ci.yml that installs with the project's install command and runs npm test (and npm run build when a build exists) on push and pull_request.

entries.name: Environment-based configuration
entries.description: PORT, DATA_DIR and credentials come from the environment, never from source.

entries.name: Health and readiness checks
entries.description: A health path that answers 2xx once the app is ready.

entries.name: Structured logging
entries.description: JSON logs with levels and request ids.
entries.blocker: No verification of log structure exists yet.
entries.next: Capture preview logs and check their structure.

entries.name: Database migrations
entries.blocker: Needs a supported SQL database (FeltDB's declared model is deployed by the app itself and needs no separate migrations).
entries.next: Support PostgreSQL or SQLite first.

entries.name: Security checks
entries.description: The factory's security scan of the code (secrets, dangerous patterns).

entries.name: Performance benchmarks
entries.blocker: No benchmark harness or thresholds for generated apps.
entries.next: Define a benchmark command and how its results are judged.

entries.name: Deployment configuration
entries.description: A start command that honours PORT, and DEPLOY.md.

profiles.name: Quick prototype
profiles.description: The factory's default: a full-stack Node app with a plain HTML UI, AppPort and tests.

profiles.name: Production web application
profiles.description: React + Vite + TypeScript UI, durable FeltDB state, AppPort, integration tests, Docker and CI.

profiles.name: Python backend
profiles.description: A FastAPI service on PostgreSQL. Not executable yet: Python and PostgreSQL are catalog-only (see their blockers).

profiles.name: Multi-service application
profiles.description: Several services in one repository. Not executable yet: monorepo support is catalog-only.

profiles.name: Existing application enhancement
profiles.description: Keep what the repository has; the factory records what it finds and adds only what you select.
